name: Agenda
description: A conference programme from one table - a chronological list, a multi-track timetable, or a now-and-next screen for the door - and a real .ics of every session.

inputs.label: Event
inputs.help: Printed at the head of every layout, and it names the exported file.

inputs.label: Venue or strapline
inputs.help: One line under the event name. A venue, a city, or the line the programme is sold on.

inputs.label: Sessions
inputs.help: One row per session. Date is YYYY-MM-DD and the times are 24-hour; leave Ends empty and the session runs an hour. Track is what splits the timetable into columns - leave it empty and the session spans every track. Kind takes session, keynote, workshop, break or social; anything else is treated as a session and printed as you typed it. Paste the whole grid from a spreadsheet to replace it.

inputs.label: Layout
inputs.help: All three read the same way: time down the page, tracks across it. The timetable gives every row the height of its real length, the list gives each row the height its words need, and the board is a screen for the door.

inputs.label: Programme style
inputs.help: All styles keep the active design system’s type and track colours. Night gives foyer screens a dark background; Minimal uses less ink on paper.

inputs.label: Pretend the time is
inputs.help: Leave empty and the board follows the clock on the device showing it. Set a moment and the board is frozen there, so a saved link and an exported picture always show the same thing.

inputs.label: Time zone
inputs.help: An IANA name such as Europe/Berlin or Australia/Brisbane. It only affects the .ics: with a zone the calendar file carries real moments in time, and without one it carries floating times that read the same in every zone.

inputs.label: Tighter spacing
inputs.help: Smaller type and less air between rows, for a programme too long for one sheet.

inputs.label: Name for sessions with no track
inputs.help: A session with an empty Track cell belongs to everybody: it spans every column of the timetable and is listed under this name.

guide.title: From a spreadsheet to a programme

tracks.label: Build the programme
steps: Put your programme in a spreadsheet with the same nine columns, then copy the whole block and paste it into **Sessions**. The paste replaces the grid, headings and all.

**Track** is what makes the columns: every different word you use becomes its own column, in the order the words first appear, and each one takes a colour from your design system. Two sessions at the same time sit side by side, never one above the other.
Leave **Track** empty for anything that belongs to everybody - a keynote, a break, the party. Those span the whole width.
Switch **Layout** to **List** when the words matter more than the clock, or to **Board** for a screen by the door.

tracks.label: Hand it out
steps: Export **PDF** for the printed programme - the page is A4 portrait, and the size fields in the export panel take any other paper.
Export **ICS** and every session becomes a calendar entry, one per row, with the room as the location and the track as its category.

Fill in **Time zone** before you export the .ics if the programme is being read from another country. Without it the times float, which is what you want for a printed handout and wrong for an invitation.
